name: requestAnimationFrame timing
plain: Runs code before each screen refresh, and reveals the display's refresh rate.
meaning: A site can learn your monitor's refresh rate (60, 120, 144 Hz) by counting frames, and can tell when the tab is hidden because callbacks stop. It is the core of smooth animation.

access.persistence: Per page; callbacks run once per display refresh while the tab is visible
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Per frame; hidden iframes stop receiving callbacks
steps: Browser calls back before the next paint

limits.headline: Can run code before each screen refresh and learn your refresh rate
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page shows animation
can: Count frames to learn your screen runs at 60, 120 or 144 Hz
Tell when the tab is hidden, since the calls pause
cannot: Run while the tab is hidden in most browsers
Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A page runs code right before each screen refresh, which also reveals your display's refresh rate.

marketing.name: requestAnimationFrame
marketing.pitch: Tells the browser to run animation code just before the next screen refresh, for smooth motion.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. It is why animations and games look smooth. When you switch tabs, the browser pauses it to save power. It also shows how fast your screen refreshes.
story.for_makers: It is the heartbeat of every browser game and animation. It lets code draw in time with the screen and pause when hidden. The timing also reveals the refresh rate, which is a small device clue.

use_cases.example: A browser game like Krunker.io calls it every frame to move players and draw the scene.
A design tool redraws only when needed, in step with the screen, so panning stays smooth.
A web map redraws tiles and labels in each frame while you drag.
A video player draws overlays like subtitles in time with each frame.
An ad script uses frame timing to check the ad was truly on screen and not hidden in a background tab.
A bot detector sees that frames never run, a sign of a hidden or headless browser.
A science site animates a simulation, like planets in orbit, smoothly at the screen's speed.

technical_bounds: Callbacks pause entirely in background tabs and hidden iframes in all major browsers (no hidden polling)
Frame rate follows the display: 60 Hz gives about 16.7 ms between callbacks, 120 Hz gives about 8.3 ms
Safari on iOS in Low Power Mode drops callbacks to about 30 fps
Timestamps are rounded like performance.now() (coarse, with jitter)
No access to the exact refresh rate; it must be measured

abuse: Detecting hidden tabs or low power mode
